title: Lesson clip comparison
purpose: An invited convenience pilot of visual reading preference and feasibility, not a test of learning efficacy, accessibility, safety or editing time saved.
initial_recruitment_target: 8-12 real adult volunteers, preferably people who watch or make screen-recorded lessons; capacity 96 invitations is not an achieved sample size.
allocation: Cryptographically shuffled blocks of 12: six lesson-order permutations crossed with two A/B orientations. A is the first exposure. First-exposure reading answer is locked before B. Mapping is hidden in the participant UI and revealed after submission. No analyst blinding or population-random sampling claim.
primary_analysis: Among all non-withdrawn, submitted independent-volunteer records before the fixed cutoff, count participant-level edited-majority, source-majority and no-majority preferences across the three cases. A majority requires that variant to be preferred in at least two of the three assigned cases. Same/neither/skipped contribute no vote. Include all-skip records as no-majority, identify missingness. Do not treat three clips as three independent participants. Report project-team responses separately.
secondary_analysis: Report case-level A/B-decoded preferences, ties, neither choices, reading accuracy after the randomized first exposure, descriptive answer latency after playback, paired distraction ratings, perceived missing information, starts/completions/skips and playback failures. Preserve negative and inconclusive outcomes. No significance testing, claimed learning gain, general efficacy or measured editing-time saving.
quality_assurance: Server-issued QA invitations write to qa-results and never enter human counts. One immutable submission per invitation. Invitations do not independently authenticate personhood; recruitment/self-report and duplicate limitations must be disclosed.
privacy: No name, email, voice, camera recording or application-retained IP address. Structured anonymous answers, coarse device class, team relationship and lesson-making experience only. Private raw records expire through a prefix-scoped S3 lifecycle after 30 days; aggregate reports may be retained. A participant can exclude a response using the same invite. No public raw-results endpoint.
playback: Existing source/edit clips only, no demo recording or new narration. Matched silent lossless VP9 study renditions must roundtrip every native sample and match pinned-Linux teaching digests. Manual playback, no autoplay. Browser-reported playback events are feasibility telemetry, not proof of attention. Record unreadable/unsupported skips rather than silently excluding them.
